ideas.name: Microsoft Corporation

The July 23 Nasdaq selloff driven by Alphabet/Tesla contagion appears to have created an unwarranted dislocation ahead of a confirmed July 29 earnings print that coincides with the Fed decision — a rare double catalyst. ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (Nasdaq ADR)
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 21 overnight screens with 17 high-conviction votes. Newly listed on Nasdaq (IPO July 10 at $149), SKHY faces its first-ever US earnings report on July 29 — a historically potent catalyst for price discovery. As NVIDIA's primary HBM supplier and the dominant player in a memory market where HBM shortages are guided to persist beyond 2030, SKHY is a direct AI infrastructure proxy. The consensus analyst 12-month PT is $281.67 vs. a last close of ~$165 — a ~70% upside gap — supported by net income +108% YoY, revenue +41% YoY, and server DRAM prices forecast to rise 18% in Q3 2026. Note: options liquidity is limited given the recency of the listing; stock purchase is the primary vehicle — size for high post-IPO volatility.

ideas.edge: Consensus 12-month PT $281.67 vs. last close ~$165 (~70% upside from IPO price per TipRanks); net income +108% YoY, revenue +41% YoY; server DRAM prices forecast +18% in Q3 2026; HBM shortage guided to persist beyond 2030; stock already pulled back from $194.80 intraday high to ~$165, well above the $149 IPO floor
ideas.bull_case: First US earnings print blows past expectations on HBM demand strength, management reaffirms scarcity guidance, and active price discovery drives SKHY toward analyst targets — the AI memory supercycle narrative finds a new liquid US vehicle.
ideas.bear_case: Post-IPO volatility is severe in both directions; any guidance disappointment or HBM pricing softness could quickly erase gains from $165; options are largely unavailable to hedge the binary event risk, leaving holders with unhedged stock exposure.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation

ideas.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
ideas.thesis: XLE appeared in 3 of 21 overnight screens as a macro hedge and catch-up trade. Brent crude is trading near $94–100/bbl on active US-Iran escalation and simultaneous Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint disruptions, yet energy equities (XOM, CVX) have underperformed the oil price move — up only ~10% vs. crude +50%+ over the conflict period — creating a valuation gap. XLE also serves as a natural portfolio hedge: it benefits directly if persistent oil-driven inflation forces a hawkish Fed surprise that pressures QQQ/tech. A binary resolution risk exists from Pakistan-China-mediated Iran peace talks reported July 24.
ideas.catalyst: Ongoing US-Iran conflict with Brent at ~$94–100/bbl; FOMC decision July 28–29 (hawkish surprise would amplify energy's inflation-hedge appeal); potential binary peace-talk resolution in coming days/weeks
ideas.edge: Energy equities up only ~10% vs. crude +50%+ over the conflict period — significant lag to commodity; Brent up ~3.4% in a single session to $94/bbl with multi-chokepoint supply disruption; XLE is options-liquid for defined-risk geopolitical exposure without single-stock concentration
ideas.bull_case: Iran conflict intensifies or drags on, Brent holds above $90, and energy equities close the gap with the commodity move — XLE call options provide leveraged, defined-risk exposure to the catch-up trade and serve as a natural inflation hedge if the Fed turns hawkish.
ideas.bear_case: Iran peace talks succeed rapidly, Brent reverses sharply, and the oil-supply-risk premium collapses — XLE and energy equities would sell off meaningfully; the geopolitical peace-talk headline risk is a known binary that could move quickly against the position.
